entries.description: Synchronizes all AAIF Working Group (wg-*) and foundation repositories, meeting minutes, charters, monthly reports, deliverables, reference architectures, and open pull requests from https://github.com/aaif/* into Google NotebookLM (https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/3f4ea1ea-fe19-4afe-8cbe-ac5f9950412d). Features full state-based lifecycle management (skip unchanged, update modified, add new, remove deleted/merged) with gcert LOAS validation, bi-weekly lookback synthesis, and automated public GitHub Gist reporting.

Write, rewrite, or review technical prose (blog posts, articles, design docs, PR descriptions, system architectures, and social posts) in Alan Blount's authentic voice: the Pragmatic Builder. Combines 20+ years of software engineering experience with DevRel clarity, dry observational wit, subtle "muppet" warmth/enthusiasm, crisp analogies, and strict anti-AI discipline (no em-dashes, no buzzword fluff, no chatbot patterns). Use whenever asked to write in Alan's tone, sound like Alan, humanize text to his personal standards, or write developer-facing content for his projects.

Create production-grade, synchronous terminal recordings (asciinema .cast) and interactive tabbed web walkthroughs for AI agents, developer tools, and CLI journeys. Includes PTY prompt-synchronization, intelligent time-compression, secret redaction, scenario banner structuring, and zoomable Mermaid flowchart companions.
Capture Critical User Journey (CUJ) screenshots and GIFs from web apps using headless Chromium. Use when you need to create visual demos, verify UI changes, or document user flows.

Synthesizes AI and developer ecosystem intelligence by combining Plushcap MCP (tech company engineering blogs, YouTube metrics, Hacker News activity, competitive spaces, and industry trend topics) with Good AI List (19,500+ open-source AI repositories, daily/weekly star velocity, developer activity, and category taxonomies). Use when asked to investigate AI tech trends, discover fast-growing open-source AI projects or breakout GitHub repositories, research tech company engineering momentum or blog activity, lookup items on goodailist.com or Plushcap, track developer metrics, analyze competitive spaces, or cross-reference enterprise tech announcements with open-source ecosystem adoption. Don't use for generic non-tech web search (use search_web) or single-file git operations (use vcs).

Create branded architecture, IT current-state, flowchart, sequence, state machine, ER/data model, timeline, swimlane, quadrant, radar/spider, loop/flywheel, nested, tree, org chart, layer stack, Venn, pyramid/funnel, bar, line, Gantt and scatter charts, high-level, process, medallion, data flow, DP integration, or DP security matrix diagrams as standalone Material Design 3 HTML/SVG/PNG with subtle Google colors. Redraw .drawio/.drawio.png/.drawio.svg or Mermaid .mmd sources at a chosen size/detail; onboard brand tokens from a website; add semantic patterns, callouts, accessible motion, or sketchy/hand-drawn styling.
Elixir coding standards and best practices. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring Elixir code to ensure idiomatic patterns, proper error handling, and Phoenix conventions.
Full engineering lifecycle — define what done means, debug systematically, verify through real surfaces before claiming completion.

Alan's standard workflow to produce a high-impact, viral X Article for the @GoogleCloudTech brand account from a trend, architecture pattern, repo, or launch: connect the trend to Google Cloud Agent Platform + live developer context, propose title/hook angles first, draft to the proven structure in Alan's Pragmatic Builder voice (20-year dev experience, muted "muppet" warmth, dry technical wit, parenthetical asides, zero em-dashes, and strict anti-AI discipline), generate dark-mode hand-drawn diagrams, and publish to a Google Doc on approval. Use whenever Alan wants to draft an X Article, turn a trend/spec/repo into an article, or brainstorm @GoogleCloudTech content angles.

Rewrite AI-sounding text so it reads naturally without changing what it says. Use when editing or reviewing prose for inflated claims, sales language, vague sources, repetitive structure, stock AI words, passive voice, filler, or chatbot artifacts. Based on Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing."

Identify, draft, validate, and refine product intent and plan specifications using Narrative-Driven Development (NDD) taxonomy. Use when designing new features, refining requirements, or preparing specs for AI agents.

Define, create, and validly measure the quality of Manim explainer videos. Use when producing technical explainer videos, defining a visual style, reviewing a render, or building/validating an LLM-based video quality grader. Covers the 3Blue1Brown-inspired visual style system, shared storytelling vocabulary, a testable quality spec, and evaluation datasets that measure whether your grader can actually see what it claims to judge.

Automates creating and lifecycle tracking of customer meeting Expert Requests in Salesforce (Vector Lightning) for Cloud AI OPM. Use when logging customer engagements, filing meeting records, or driving browser automation for Salesforce Expert Request creation and status completion.
Write and test Storybook stories for React components. Use for component isolation, visual testing, and documentation.
Full-stack UI development workflow with component isolation, testing, visual documentation, and CUJ capture. Use for React/TypeScript frontend development.

Grant a teammate WRITE (push) access to the OPM skills repo (or any FoG / GitHub Enterprise repo) so they can contribute skills. Use when asked to add someone as a contributor or collaborator, to give push/write access, or to onboard a colleague to the repo. This is a deterministic action: the agent just runs the bundled script — no reasoning, minimal tokens. Don't use for read access (public FoG repos are already readable by anyone onboarded) or for creating a repo.

Research skill to match Google Cloud Customers and Opportunities to their account team (FSR, KAE, CE, FDE, TAM) and active products being used via a parallel modular engine or grounded lookups across authoritative internal webapps: go/kerrigan and go/vector, alongside Moma search. Use when researching customer account leadership, deal context, billing/product workload footprints, or assembling field engagement tables and distribution lists. Features decoupled authentication configurations that execute independently across available SSO, LOAS, and Workspace tool paths.

Create, time-compress, redact, and share studio-grade terminal recordings (.cast) and interactive 2-tab web walkthroughs for AI agents and CLI tools. Use when producing customer-facing demos, executive walk-throughs, field enablement videos, or GitHub Pages demo players without live demo failures or dead-air latency.

Broadcasts ONE structured announcement to the Google Cloud field (sellers and SEs) across many Google Chat rooms in a single consistent house format (🚨 header + intro + Scope + Action Item + links + footer). Drafts the message with the user, recommends target rooms from the OPM room-directory spreadsheets, forces a sandbox preview, and only broadcasts after explicit approval of BOTH the message and the room list. Use when broadcasting a field announcement, an EAP / launch / GA / roadmap update, a DRZ / data-residency update, or posting the same message to many field or community rooms at once. Don't use for one-off DMs, replying inside an existing thread, non-field internal posts, or a message to a single room (post that directly with the gchat skill). Reuses: gchat, gchat-conduct, chat-conversation, opm, gsheets, gdrive.

Formats a short, BLUF-first escalation to PMs when a customer issue or bug needs product-team attention. Use when asked to escalate a customer bug/blocker to PMs, write a concise escalation, or draft a short escalation email/message in the Background/Problem/Ask structure with client name, numbers, and bug links. Don't use for weekly notes, field broadcasts, or general status reports.

Build a sharp, on-brand Google Cloud AI Platform slide deck (Gemini Enterprise / field enablement) from a source doc or topic, by copying the official brand templates and filling them with a render-verify loop. Use when asked to create/build/design a deck, presentation, or slides for the field, an EBC, a launch, or a product/topic overview in the Google Cloud AI brand style. Covers layout selection (title, agenda, 3-column key-takeaways, big-statement, divider, content, FAQ, closing), title/text sizing so nothing wraps or overlaps, sourcing REAL images/diagrams (from the source doc + brand image library, never generated), and verifying each slide by rendering it. Don't use for non-Google-brand decks, for editing an existing deck's copy only, or for analyst/RFP writing.

Simulate and validate developer interactions with GCP platform tools and Google agent skills across auth tiers (Tier 0 Zero Auth, Tier 1 API Keys, Tier 2/3 Managed GCP ADC/SA). Use when designing cross-product Google AI tools, auditing user consent and opt-out flows, testing fallback to offline skills, or verifying ARD catalog discovery without runtime crashes.
Process Gemini meeting-notes emails (from gemini-notes@google.com):

Use when an OPM wants to audit their own recent activity (default last 4 weeks) and produce a manager-facing "Activity Map & Priorities" Google Doc. It mines the RUNNING USER's own data — their AI-platform session history (e.g. CloudCode, GE App, Cowork, gogo), Google Calendar, Gmail and Drive — time-weights the work into a shared set of OPM task categories (customer-facing, field enablement, PM-facing, analyst relations, product testing, content, AI productivity, team ops), optionally splits by product, proposes OKR-anchored priorities, and fills the team template so every OPM's doc looks the same for the manager. Triggers: "map my activity", "what do I spend my time on", "build my activity / priorities doc for my manager", "time audit", "categorize my work". NOT for triaging a live to-do list, and NOT for personal (non-work) projects. Uses the user's own accounts only.

Toolkit for an Outbound Product Manager (OPM) working on the Gemini Enterprise APP (GE App) surface. Use when answering field/seller/customer questions about GE App, finding the authoritative GE App source (FAQ, pricing, battlecard, roadmap dates, DRZ, EAP), drafting field comms or replies as an OPM, or posting in the GE/OPM Google Chat rooms. Grounds every answer in the OPM-validated GE App knowledge base (the "Leia grounding" set) and applies GE App audience rules (INTERNAL_STRICT / INTERNAL_NDA / EXTERNAL_SAFE). Answers in two tiers: the OPM-validated source of truth first, then an optional, clearly-labelled "field signal" complement read from internal GE/field chat rooms (interesting but unvalidated, never passed off as official). Don't use for GE Agent Platform deep-dives, for Gemini for Workspace, or for analyst RFP/Gartner writing (use the gartner-responses skill for that). Depends on: google_workspace (CSA + Docs/Sheets/Drive), gchat, gchat-conduct.

Turn customer / field inputs into a PM-facing **PM Requirements Brief** — a concise, executive-length (1–2 page) decision doc for the product team, as a Google Doc (usually one living doc with one subject per tab) or a slide deck. For a given requirement it states: scope, what the requirement demands, the lifecycle + validation gate, what customers do today, the Cloud Blockers (with PM status and CR counts), customer examples, and phased improvement suggestions for PMs. Use when an OPM needs to structure a requirement (a regulatory need, a governance gap, a missing capability) from customer inputs and present it to PMs, grounded in Buganizer Cloud Blockers and cited sources. Works for any customer and any topic; customers appear only as examples. Also fires on "customer requirements brief". Don't use for field/seller comms or analyst RFPs.

Simulate and verify AI coding agents (OpenCode, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor) interacting with tools and CLI environments inside hermetic Podman/Docker containers. Use when evaluating agent developer journeys (CUJs), testing multi-turn sessions without polluting your local workstation, or creating reproducible sandboxes for customer agent demos.
